items.title: Show HN: Banking Access Index – 19 US banking providers, 8 countries, CC-BY
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.globalsolo.global/data/banking-access-index Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49445908 Points: 8 # Comments: 6
items.content:
Which US business banking providers actually accept founders who live outside the US — documented from provider-published sources, not anecdotes. 19 providers, 239 claims that survived independent re-verification against the original source pages. Where a provider publishes nothing, the cell says so instead of guessing.

JSON carries the full evidence quotes · CSV is the acceptance matrix

Re-verified quarterly against the source pages. Leave an email to get the diff when cells change — which providers opened, which closed, with the new source quotes.

39 of the 152 country cells resolve to unknown. Reviewing them together showed they were not one state but four, and the difference changes what you should do next — so every unknown cell now carries a second field naming which one it is, and a citation recording where we looked. “We could not find it” is only useful to you if you can see where we searched.

61 cells resolve to restricted, and only 9 of them name the country on a published prohibited list. In 40, the provider names no country anywhere — the bar comes from a blanket rule such as “US citizens or permanent residents only”. The answer you get is the same in both cases, and it is correct in both. What differs is how much is published about you specifically, which is what you need if you plan to ask the provider or appeal. So each restricted cell now names its evidence type too.

Hover any cell for the underlying note. Country columns describe the founder's country of residence , not the LLC's state of formation. Full evidence quotes are in the JSON download and in each provider's detail card below.

Details column — one icon per dimension of the provider's card: owner ID, account rails, receiving from abroad, card issuance, onboarding, phone & 2FA. Color tracks the published state: green = published positive , amber = conditional or partial , red = published restriction , gray = no published statement . Hover for the value; click to jump to the cited sources.

items.title: BMW iX3, in Cina è più grande ma costa quasi 29.000 euro in meno
items.summary: BMW lancia in Cina la iX3 L a passo lungo: più spazio, batterie e software dedicati e prezzi da circa 34.400 euro
items.content:
A guardarla bene sembra la stessa auto che abbiamo imparato a conoscere in questi mesi. Stesso nome, design ricalcato e appartenenza alla Neue Klasse, la nuova generazione di vetture elettriche prodotte dal costruttore bavarese. Eppure, tra la BMW iX3 europea e la nuova BMW iX3 L destinata alla Cina esiste un abisso.La Casa tedesca ha infatti svelato la variante a passo lungo del suo SUV a batteria, un modello pensato esclusivamente per il contesto del Dragone che non solo offre più spazio a bordo, ma arriva sul mercato con prezzi che farebbero gola a molti automobilisti del Vecchio Continente.

Più lunga e più spaziosa

In Cina lo spazio per i passeggeri posteriori continua a essere un elemento determinante nella scelta di un'auto premium. Non sorprende quindi che BMW abbia allungato il passo della nuova iX3 fino a 3.005 millimetri, ben 108 millimetri in più rispetto alla versione destinata all'Europa.La lunghezza complessiva sale così a 4,88 metri, con l'obiettivo di incrementare soprattutto l'abitabilità della seconda fila. Una soluzione già vista su numerose berline e SUV premium destinati al mercato cinese. La produzione avverrà nello stabilimento di Shenyang, mentre le iX3 europee continueranno a uscire dalla fabbrica ungherese di Debrecen.

Batterie diverse per abbassare il prezzo

La vera sorpresa, come dicevamo, arriva osservando la scheda tecnica. La versione d'ingresso iX3 30L utilizza una batteria LFP (litio-ferro-fosfato) da 77 kWh, una tecnologia generalmente meno costosa rispetto alle celle NMC adottate sui modelli europei.Anche la potenza è inferiore: 265 CV contro i 320 CV della iX3 40 sDrive destinata all'Europa. Una scelta che consente a BMW di contenere i costi senza compromettere eccessivamente le prestazioni. Salendo di livello troviamo invece la iX3 40L xDrive da 374 CV, dotata di doppio motore e trazione integrale, mentre al vertice della gamma si colloca la iX3 50L xDrive, che promette numeri da riferimento per il segmento.

Il prezzo che fa discutere

È tuttavia il listino che fa discutere più di ogni altra faccenda. In Cina la BMW iX3 30L parte da circa 34.400 euro, mentre la 40L xDrive si ferma intorno ai 38.200 euro. La top di gamma 50L xDrive costa invece circa 43.300 euro.Numeri impressionanti se confrontati con quelli europei. In Germania, infatti, la nuova iX3 viene proposta a partire da 63.400 euro, mentre la versione più ricca supera i 70.000 euro. La differenza sfiora quindi i 29.000 euro, una cifra sufficiente per acquistare un'altra auto di media taglia.

La sfida cinese cambia tutto

Dietro questa strategia c'è una realtà ormai evidente: il mercato cinese è diventato il terreno di scontro più competitivo dell'industria automobilistica mondiale. BMW deve confrontarsi con rivali locali sempre più aggressivi come Xiaomi, che propone il SUV elettrico YU7 a un prezzo inferiore, e con una Tesla Model Y che in Cina costa meno della stessa iX3 d'ingresso.Per restare competitiva, la Casa tedesca ha quindi sviluppato una versione profondamente localizzata, con software dedicati, integrazione con l'ecosistema digitale cinese e una struttura dei costi completamente diversa rispetto a quella europea. Il risultato è una BMW che porta lo stesso nome del modello destinato al mercato delle nostre latitudini, ma che nei fatti racconta una storia molto diversa.[drivek_widget brand_id="bmw" model_id="serie-3-touring"]

items.title: Value Classes Still Need Compiler Sympathy
items.summary: Article URL: https://johan-sjolen.github.io/post/compiler-sympathy/compiler-sympathy/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49445884 Points: 17 # Comments: 5
items.content:
JEP 401 , a major Valhalla milestone, has been integrated as a preview feature in JDK 28. This is very exciting, as value classes increase both our ability to communicate the semantics of our programs to others and the optimization opportunities available to the JVM.

However, I have seen people online essentially taking a "Value all the classes!" approach to this. I worry that there is a belief that ordinary classes give you a floor on performance, and that value classes will do their best to raise you above that floor, but won't ever take you below it. Unfortunately, that is not true. A well-intentioned program may put the JVM into a situation where a flattened representation is faster for some methods, and a reference representation is faster for others. When these methods interact, the JVM is forced to convert between the two representations. I want value classes to be more than just magic, so today I am going to show you what the JVM is capable of right now , and where its limitations are. I hope that with this you'll have some context for reasoning about the code that you (or your AI agent) write.

The main optimization advantage of value classes is that we give up identity. This gives the JVM freedom to choose a suitable representation for a particular situation. Without the requirement of identity, the runtime can more readily flatten values (avoiding pointer chasing), scalarize them by representing their components independently in registers or on the stack. For the value object itself, escape analysis becomes trivial: there is no identity whose escape must be proven unobservable.

We are going to examine three examples: a large final value stored flat, a direct value transformation compiled without allocation, and a generic virtual call that requires materialization.

JEP 539 , Strict Field Initialization in the JVM, lets the JVM rely on a final field having been initialized before its enclosing object becomes observable. Because such a field cannot later be updated, the JVM may use a non-atomic flattened layout without risking a torn assignment. Mutable fields, however, must preserve tear-free assignment. If a mutable field contains a value that is too large for an atomic flattened update, the JVM must instead use a reference layout. The strict-initialization guarantee opens up many optimization possibilities.

FourLongs has 32 bytes of payload, making it too large for an atomic flattened update in the current JVM. But Envelope.payload is a record component and therefore a strictly initialized final field: once initialized, it is never updated. The JVM is consequently free to store payload using a non-atomic flattened layout. In the current Valhalla master build, the field-layout diagnostic reports the following when using PrintFieldLayout :

Here we can see that a FourLongs consists of its four components and a 1-byte null marker, and that it supports a nullable, non-atomic flattened layout. The runtime uses this fact in the Envelope record, and allows FourLongs to be flattened. The key point is that Envelope is also immutable; the layout would have to change if we replaced it with a mutable class:

Why is that? Let's consider a data race between two threads:

Writing a flattened field requires writing its individual components. If thread1 and thread2 wrote those components independently, another thread could observe a torn value such as (1, 1, 0, 0) , assembled from parts of two different assignments. The Java Memory Model forbids such tearing: after both threads have joined, this program may print only (1, 0, 0, 0) or (0, 1, 0, 0) . Guaranteeing tear-free assignment for a flattened value this large would be expensive, so the current JVM uses a reference layout. Each thread constructs a complete FourLongs and then performs an atomic reference store.

If we have a small function that changes a component in a loop, like this:

At the source level, we can see that every call to bumpA constructs a new FourLongs . At the call site of run , however, we can see that the returned value is effectively only there to change the a component of value . A good optimizing compiler ought to be able to recognize that as well. It turns out that C2 is a pretty good compiler! C2 keeps the representation scalarized, and it even recognizes that the final result must be iterations + (2 + 3 + 4) = iterations + 9 when iterations >= 0 . The following is an abridged excerpt of the generated code:

If we keep bumpA unchanged but make FourLongs an identity record, C2 must prove that its identity has no impact on the computation. Compilers can often do this, but now we depend on the compiler proving it in each case. When I tried to do this (by removing value from the FourLongs declaration), C2 was not capable of performing this optimization.

The following is an abridged excerpt of C2's compilation of IdentityRecordExperiment::run . The allocation remains in run 's loop even though bumpA has been inlined:

Clearly, providing the compiler with stronger semantic guarantees can sometimes produce a very big win.

Now we are going to look at something a bit more complex. This example is derived from an email we received from a user on the valhalla-dev mailing list. He had ported a parsing library from Elm to Java and noticed a slowdown after converting all of his records to value records. A performance regression is obviously not the result we want, but an unexpected result like this is fascinating: value classes give the JVM more semantic information and greater freedom, so how could using them make the program slower? I did a deep dive to find the cause and a source-level fix. This investigation has opened up an interesting compiler problem that my colleagues on the C2 team are now actively investigating. I'll explain my findings here, but please keep in mind that I've had to simplify this greatly. The JVM and javac are both fairly complex, so I have to leave out details.

This is pretty simple code. We have multiple Frobber s that take a LargeValue and produce a Carrier , which contains another LargeValue . The Frobber interface extends the Fun interface.

Let's look at this through the lens of the JVM so that we can understand what is happening. Java implements generics through type erasure, replacing these type parameters with Object . That means that Frobber effectively inherits this method as far as the JVM is concerned:

The typed signature Carrier apply(LargeValue) does not appear in the inherited JVM method descriptor and therefore has to be recovered through dynamic analysis. To accommodate this type discrepancy, javac generates bridge methods in the class file. Each implementation gains a method approximately equivalent to this:

The bridge accepts the erased argument, casts it to the expected type, and invokes the method we actually wrote. Now consider the method from the original reproducer:

There are two separate interface call sites here. If each call site only observes one implementation, C2 can devirtualize it. For example, the first call site might always receive a FrobIt , while the second always receives a GrobIt . C2 can independently guard and inline both targets. In this experiment, C2 managed to remove all heap allocations. In pseudo-Java, the result looks like this. We represent scalarized values (values that are not heap references) by appending Fields to the type name:

At this level, there is no longer a call to the generated bridge. Devirtualizing and inlining the target also inlines its bridge. Once the bridge has disappeared into the surrounding compilation, there is no longer a real Object apply(Object) call boundary.

In the report we received, however, the call sites were megamorphic. In our example, that means FrobIt , GrobIt , and DrobIt were all called interchangeably. With three hot implementations at each call site, C2 leaves the calls dynamically dispatched:

The inherited method descriptor defines an ABI that requires callers to pass object references and implementations to return object references.

The caller currently has a scalarized LargeValue , but Object apply(Object) cannot accept four independent scalar components. It requires a genuine reference. The caller must therefore materialize the value before making the call.

The dynamically selected bridge then has to translate in the other direction:

The bridge casts the incoming reference to LargeValue , extracts its components, and invokes the typed implementation using the scalarized value-object calling convention. The typed implementation returns a scalarized Carrier , but the bridge itself promises to return Object , so it must materialize the result before returning.

The megamorphic version of reproduce therefore looks approximately like this:

The bridge is acting as an ABI adapter. On one side is the erased Object apply(Object) calling convention. On the other is the typed Carrier apply(LargeValue) calling convention, where value components can be passed and returned in scalarized form.

As you can imagine, this is very expensive. At each call, the caller has to turn a scalarized value into an object reference, which means materializing the value on the heap. It cannot simply point the callee at temporary stack storage: the call is opaque, so the callee may retain the reference and access it after the caller returns. The argument must therefore be a GC-managed heap object.

items.title: Oldinsurancemaps.net is now a Charter Project
items.summary: Article URL: https://openstreetmap.us/news/2026/08/oim-charter-project/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49445873 Points: 43 # Comments: 3
items.content:
OSM US is incredibly excited to announce the latest Charter Project: OldInsuranceMaps.net (OIM)!

If you’re a map nerd you’ll remember ever seeing a Sanborn Insurance Map in person. They often come in absolutely massive tomes that were once perhaps the closest you could get to OpenStreetMap before the digital age; over the years, each page becomes a collage of small cutouts of paper pasted over streets since renamed, or buildings since demolished. They are both beautiful pieces of artwork and one of the most accurate references for geographic data in the United States from 1867 into the 1960s. Sanborn Maps are a valuable resource for historical mappers and researchers (as briefly mentioned in our OpenHistoricalMap Mapper Highlight post), and thanks to OIM their georeferenced information is much more accessible.

A Sanborn map of Richmond, Virginia at the Library of Congress. Notice where paper cutouts have been layered over the original map.

Adam Cox began OIM while at Louisiana State University back in 2022 and today the platform hosts over 1200 Sanborn maps primarily sourced from the Library of Congress. These maps have such broad appeal that a wide range of people have been drawn to the project, from hobbyists exploring the history of their hometown to scholars undertaking large research studies and professionals working on redevelopment. It is very likely that a place that you care about can be explored via OIM, and there is a strong community of volunteer georeferencers to connect with (in case you need another mapping rabbit hole to fall down).

Anyone can request that their city or town’s Sanborn map(s) be added to the website. Scanned maps can then be georeferenced by placing ground control points and digitally stitching each page together. Thanks to Adam’s work, the interface is intuitive to learn and accessible no matter your existing knowledge of geography and GIS. It’s an innovative combination of historical archivism, open-sourced technology, and crowdsourced knowledge.

Sanborn maps at the New Orleans Public Library, CIty Archives and Special Collections

Our project exists to facilitate the creation of open historical map materials, and to do so in a way that is accessible, engaging, and robust. Becoming part of the Charter Project program is the perfect way to bring this work to the next level, because the ethos of the OSM US organization (and all the great people within it!) resonates so strongly with what our platform is all about.

OIM joins YouthMappers, Yesterdays, and OpenHistoricalMap as an OSM US Charter Project. In particular, the OSM US team is excited to see increased collaboration and synergies between OHM, Yesterdays, and OIM. Each tool is individually excellent at collecting and portraying historic geographic data, and many contributors to one platform naturally include another in their workflows. For example, mappers contributing to OHM already create georeferenced mosaics on OldInsuranceMaps.net and use them directly while editing OHM as historical reference layers to trace from, and Yesterdays includes Sanborn maps from OIM as a base layer to help users place historical images accurately.

University of Richmond student with a digital display built with the help of OldInsuranceMaps.net

Georeference some maps and explore the site! Get started at oldinsurancemaps.net

Any project in the OpenStreetMap ecosystem is invited to apply to become a Charter Project; applications are always open and reviewed on a rolling basis. Visit the Community & Charter Projects page to learn more.

Our Community Project and Charter Project programs provide a long-term home for notable OpenStreetMap tools, programs, and services. We provide projects with stable legal and fiscal frameworks so developers and organizers can focus on what they do best: building things.

items.content:
Voleva acquistare una PlayStation 5 a 199 euro su Vinted, e invece l'affare si è trasformato in una colossale truffa che è costata 11.000 euro ad un giovane romano. Il raggiro era stato organizzato minuziosamente, eccetto un particolare: è bastato un ordine di due pizze da asporto per aiutare i Carabinieri a rintracciare i malviventi.

BONIFICI RIPETUTI

items.title: Canada's retaliation tests the limit of American power under Trump
items.summary: The president is using US dominance to challenge allies and enemies alike - but both Canada and Iran have found ways to fight back.
items.content:
Two days before US-Canada trade talks dramatically derailed, Vice-President JD Vance was telling an audience at a private fundraiser that Prime Minister Mark Carney was a "very sweet guy".

In a private audio recording leaked to the Canadian Press, Vance reportedly went on to say that Carney "comes in and puffs his chest out and says: 'I'm going to, like, out-tough Donald Trump.'"

He described that approach as "hilarious" because the Canadians ultimately "climb down on a lot of issues".

Maybe those comments, which received considerable coverage in Canada, were not the proximate cause for Carney's diplomats to pack up and go home over the weekend. But they certainly didn't help.

Carney's move abruptly terminated negotiations over a new trade agreement and sparked a fresh round of tariffs between neighbours who conduct more than $872bn (£640bn) in bilateral annual trade.

The serious and deepening rift - and Vance's comments - offer the latest example of a Trump administration willing to exert force on the global stage against friend and foe alike, again highlighting the potentially disruptive consequences of such actions.

What's more, if Trump thought the Canadians would cave in the face of American pressure - as many US allies have done over the past 19 months - he may have miscalculated. And the consequences of that mistake could linger for the rest of his presidency.

While the latest rupture is striking, friction between the US and Canada dates back to the first Trump administration and the negotiations that created the USMCA: the deal replacing the 1990s-era North American Free Trade Agreement (Nafta).

Complicating matters were personal clashes between Trump and Justin Trudeau, who was then Canada's prime minister. As Trump prepared to return to the White House in late 2024, he derisively referred to Trudeau as "governor" and to Canada as America's "51st State."

Underlying those insults was a geopolitical outlook that positioned the US primarily as a hemispheric power entitled to exert political, military, and economic influence over its immediate region – and that most definitely included Canada.

Administration officials viewed Canada as contributing too little to regional defence while disproportionately benefiting from trade with its southern neighbour.

In Trump's worldview, where economic security and national security are inextricably linked, Canada and Mexico - two of America's largest trading partners - became early, obvious targets.

'Half my business will be gone' - firms in Canada and US fear trade war

How Canada could hit back to hurt the US economy - and Trump

It's why the US president said he wanted to take over Greenland too.

"If you listen to really anybody in state, treasury, or commerce [departments], you will hear the phrase 'economic security is national security'," said Drew Delong, head of corporate statecraft at the Kearney Foresight think tank.

By the start of this year, however, as North American trade negotiations proceeded in fits and starts, Trump's attention shifted away from Canada to his military interventions in Venezuela and then the Middle East.

Across every region, though, the core line of Trump's international strategy remains consistent: the US is a dominant power capable of imposing its will for national benefit.

But power has limits. Trump's second term has been a continuous test of those limits - and, at times, a lesson in finding exactly where they are.

While obvious differences exist between a shooting war in Iran and a trade dispute with Canada, the lessons are not dissimilar. In both, the US faces a counterpart that, despite having far less overall power, retains the means to retaliate.

For Iran, that leverage lies in targeting US allies and disrupting global commerce by threatening maritime chokepoints like the Strait of Hormuz.

Canada, for its part, is beginning to test its own ability to inflict economic pain. Tuesday's targeted tariffs mark a first step. Future measures could include restricting US access to Canadian energy and critical minerals, alongside consumer boycotts of American goods.

"As the broader world shifts into a more economic security theatre, you see this game of chokepoints and leverage angles continue to pan out across supply chains," said DeLong. Countries just have to look for them, he added.

For the moment, clear exit ramps are scarce. Trump has escalated his rhetoric, repeatedly accusing Canada of "ripping off" the US, while Ontario Premier Doug Ford fired back by telling the American president to "kiss my ass".

"Every time we push allies and partners away, I think we incentivise them to look for new relationships and new partnerships rather than trying to acquiesce to US demands," said Imran Bayoumi, deputy director of the GeoStrategy Initiative at the Atlantic Council.

Still, room remains for cooler heads to prevail. Canada's new tariffs take effect in two weeks, while the most significant US retaliation - a 50% tariff on Canadian-built vehicles and auto parts - will not kick in until early 2027.

As with any conflict - economic or military - a cycle of escalation can prove difficult to break. However, the multi-month buffer before the next wave of US tariffs gives negotiators space to restart talks. Until Friday night, these had been showing some progress.

A more pressing deadline is November's US midterm elections. Democratic congressional victories could significantly curtail Trump's authority - or unexpected Republican success could embolden him further.

At present, Ottawa seems content to bet on the former outcome, calculating that fear of a midterm blowout in key industrial battlegrounds like Michigan and Ohio will force Trump to back down before ballots are cast.

"I don't think there's the kind of internal political divisions in Canada that maybe the Trump administration would have expected," Bayoumi said. "I think Carney has a lot of political runway to really get a good deal for Canada and not settle for anything less."

There is another possibility that Carney has aired publicly since Trump returned to office, however.

Canada may continue shifting away from the US altogether, charting a course that deliberately widens the distance between the two nations. As Carney noted: "We cannot depend on traditional alliances when the rules of the game have fundamentally changed."

While geographic proximity ensures the two countries will remain intertwined, the deeply integrated economic relationship of recent decades may be coming to an end.

In that respect, Canada presents a contrast with Mexico, which appears to be opting for even closer economic integration with the US. Meanwhile, other global trading partners - including US allies in Europe and Asia - are watching Canada's "elbows up" resistance as a plausible blueprint for future dealings with Trump.

"Ten years from now, this is going to be taught in classrooms," said DeLong. "You have these bifurcating paths within North America, and the question is: Are they going to come back together, or is this going to continue to split? And if it does, who benefits most in the long run?"

If the supposedly easygoing Canadians can stand up to their pugnacious – and powerful - neighbour, others may decide they can, too.

items.title: Windows 11, il tool di diagnostica WHESVC è in realtà uno spyware?
items.summary: Qualche settimana fa un tweet accusava il tool di monitorare costantemente tantissimi aspetti dell'OS, con conseguenze inevitabili per le prestazioni, e addirittura di inviare dati ogni 15 minuti a...
items.content:
Recentemente una funzionalità telemetrica di Windows 11 è stata oggetto di polemiche piuttosto accese nella community: si tratta del servizio Windows Health and Optimized Experiences, noto internamente come whesvc, che su Twitter è stato accusato di monitorare costantemente parametri come uso della CPU, temperature e stato della batteria, inviando dati a Microsoft ogni 15 minuti, con tutte le conseguenze del caso per quanto riguarda prestazioni del sistema operativo, autonomia del device e privacy dell'utente.

Un'analisi molto più approfondita, a opera di un esperto di reverse engineering, suggerisce però non solo che le accuse siano infondate, ma che il tool sia molto più complesso di quanto potrebbe sembrare in superficie. Tanto per cominciare, Xusheng Li conferma sostanzialmente quanto ha detto a lo sviluppatore di Microsoft Scott Hanselman rispondendo al tweet, e cioè che il sistema è stato progettato per raccogliere dati diagnostici quando Windows rileva rallentamenti o comportamenti anomali, archiviando le informazioni localmente affinché possano eventualmente essere condivise tramite Feedback Hub.

This was added in 2025 and is for Performance-diagnostic capture: When Windows detects slow or sluggish behavior, it can record targeted performance traces locally under %SystemRoot%\Temp\DiagOutputDir\Whesvc that can be filed with Feedback Hub. It's not laptop specific.

items.title: Disney+ e 4K, il contenzioso legale si allarga. InterDigital: "Anche usare il codec VP9 viola i nostri brevetti"
items.summary: Avviato un nuovo procedimento contro Disney. InterDigital: "A Disney chiediamo di smettere di danneggiare i clienti e trovare un accordo di lungo termine" ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
La disputa fra Disney e InterDigital non solo non accenna a risolversi ma è appena peggiorata. Perché InterDigital ha avviato un nuovo procedimento davanti all'Unified Patent Court (UPC) relativo al VP9, cioè il codec che ora Disney+ sta adottando per poter garantire, pur con molti compromessi, il 4K agli utenti abbonati al piano Premium, il più costoso. Tale opzione era stata disattivata nelle scorse settimane dopo che Disney aveva perso una disputa riguardante i brevetti sulla tecnologia di compressione HEVC detenuti proprio da InterDigital.

Per InterDigital il passaggio a un altro codec "continua a violare la nostra innovazione brevettata", ha specificato il direttore legale della società, Josh Schmidt, in una nota ufficiale . " Il problema per Disney e altri trasgressori è che, oltre a essere inferiore a HEVC, VP9 utilizza chiaramente tecnologie sviluppate da ingegneri di InterDigital e di altre aziende. E, come per qualsiasi nostra tecnologia utilizzata, ci aspettiamo di ricevere una royalty equa per il valore della nostra innovazione, dato il significativo investimento che facciamo nella nostra ricerca ".

" Abbiamo contattato Disney per la prima volta per una licenza diversi anni fa ", ricorda Schmidt. " Avremmo di gran lunga preferito concludere un accordo amichevole già allora. Ci siamo rivolti al tribunale solo perché questa strada ci era preclusa, e solo per stabilire ciò che non avrebbe dovuto essere messo in dubbio: che la nostra innovazione ha un valore significativo e che le aziende che costruiscono attività redditizie su di essa dovrebbero pagare un prezzo equo ".

Schmidt ha puntato il dito anche contro l'approccio di Disney: togliere funzionalità agli utenti piuttosto che pagare la licenza a InterDigital. " I clienti non solo vengono danneggiati dalla scelta di Disney di rimuovere alcune funzionalità dalle sue offerte, ma anche dalla perdita dei benefici derivanti dalle future innovazioni che i ricavi di un accordo di licenza avrebbero finanziato ", ha aggiunto Schmidt. " Pertanto, il nostro messaggio a Disney è lo stesso di quando abbiamo iniziato le trattative: smettetela di danneggiare i clienti e raggiungiamo un accordo a lungo termine che rifletta il giusto valore dell'innovazione che Disney utilizza quotidianamente ".

items.title: RAG Is Simpler Than You Think
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.lighthousenewsletter.com/p/rag-is-simpler-than-you-think Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49445727 Points: 49 # Comments: 24
items.content:
Nowadays, most people seem to over-engineer their RAG stack. They jump straight to embeddings, vector databases, and reranking pipelines. Meanwhile, their users just want to find the doc that says “How to reset my password.”

In engineering, there’s always the right tool for the right problem. In AI Retrieval Systems it’s not different.

Before we dive into recipes, let’s establish when you should use each approach. The key factors are:

1. Data Freshness Requirements - Real-time updates (news, social media) favor approaches with easy re-indexing. Daily or weekly updates work well with hybrid approaches. A stable corpus (monthly or quarterly updates) makes pre-embedding sensible.

2. Corpus Characteristics - High churn (more than 10% changes daily) means you should avoid full pre-embedding. Stable documents work fine with pre-embedding. Long-tail distribution (90% never accessed) means on-the-fly wins.

3. Query Patterns - Keyword-heavy queries should start with full-text search. Semantic or conversational queries benefit from embeddings. Mixed patterns need hybrid approaches.

4. Scale & Performance - Less than 1000 queries per day means simple approaches are sufficient. 1K to 10K queries per day requires selective optimization. More than 10K queries per day justifies full optimization.

5. Team Capabilities - No ML expertise means stay with full-text plus query rewriting. Some ML experience makes hybrid search manageable. Having an ML team available makes advanced approaches viable.

Now, let’s look at the recipe book. Start at the top. Move down only when you have data proving you need to.

Good old BM25. Elasticsearch. Postgres full-text search. The stuff that existed before “embedding” became a verb.

You’re just starting out. Your users write keyword-style queries (”pandas merge dataframe”) . Exact matches matter (”invoice #12345”) . You want zero ML complexity. Your corpus has proprietary terminology (more on this later) .

Zero API costs. Fast (under 10ms). Easy to debug (you can see exactly why a document matched). Surprisingly effective (handles many use cases). No chunking strategy needed – works with full documents. No evaluation complexity – easy to test and validate. No model deprecation risk (BM25 doesn’t change).

Misses synonyms (”car” vs “automobile”). Fails on semantic queries (”How do I...?”). Can’t understand intent beyond keywords.

In my experience, this handles a significant portion of use cases. Don’t skip this step. You might be surprised how far you can get.

When you jump straight to embeddings, you immediately face questions like: What chunk size? (512 tokens? 1024?) What overlap? (50 tokens? 100?) Semantic chunking or fixed-size? How do I evaluate if my chunking is good?

With full-text search, you skip all of this. Your documents are your documents. Search just works.

Use an LLM to transform messy user queries into clean keyword searches.

Most “semantic search” problems are actually query formulation problems.

Users ask questions conversationally. Vocabulary mismatch (users say “fix bugs”, docs say “debugging”). You have internal jargon (your framework called “Atlas”). You want flexibility to iterate quickly on query strategies.

An LLM can remove stopwords (”how do I” becomes nothing). It can add synonyms (”car” becomes “car automobile vehicle”). It can translate domain terms (”speed up code” becomes “optimize performance”). It can decompose complex queries (”read CSV and plot” becomes [”read CSV”, “plot data”]). It can learn from your glossary (via system prompt).

With embeddings, if results aren’t good, you need to adjust chunking strategy, re-embed entire corpus, run regression tests on your eval set, and hope it improved.

With query rewriting, if results aren’t good, you adjust the system prompt. That’s it. Test immediately.

The agent can iterate, learn, and adapt – all without re-embedding anything.

Say your company has a Python framework called “Atlas.” If you use general-purpose embeddings:

The model has no idea your “ Atlas ” exists. It falls back to what it learned in training. But with query rewriting:

For proprietary terms, exact keyword matching beats semantic understanding.

Thanks for reading Lighthouse AI! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.

Use BM25 to get candidates (top 50-100), then rerank with embeddings (top 10).

BM25 is fast and great at keyword matching. Embeddings are good at semantic understanding. Together, they cover each other’s weaknesses.

Users ask semantic questions (” find alternatives to X” ). BM25 plus query rewriting alone isn’t cutting it (you have data proving this). You can tolerate 100-500ms latency. Your corpus is relatively stable (not changing every minute).

Let’s do the math with current pricing (OpenAI text-embedding-3-small at $0.02 per 1M tokens):

Embedding 50 docs per query (avg 500 tokens each) means 50 docs × 500 tokens = 25,000 tokens

Cost: 25,000 × $0.00002 = ~$0.0005 per query. At 1,000 queries per day × 30 days = ~$15 per month.

Embedding 50 documents on-the-fly adds 200-500ms per query. For user-facing search, that’s noticeable. This is where the real trade-off lives – not cost, but speed.

When you introduce embeddings, you need to decide how to chunk your documents (fixed-size? semantic? by section?). You need to determine what chunk size and overlap to use. You need to handle chunks that span important context.

If your data changes frequently, why pay to re-embed everything?

High document churn (more than 10% of docs updated daily). Real-time content (news, social media, live updates). You’re experimenting with embedding models (no re-indexing needed). Data freshness is critical (documents must be up-to-date). Small K for reranking (20-50 docs).

Here’s something people don’t talk about enough: embedding models get deprecated .

OpenAI deprecated text-embedding-ada-002 in favor of text-embedding-3. If you pre-embedded 10 million documents with the old model, you now need to re-embed all 10 million documents with the new model, update your vector database, run regression tests on your evaluation set, validate that quality didn’t degrade, handle the cutover period, and deal with any API changes.

Latency. You’re embedding documents on every query. This is only viable if you’re okay with 200-500ms latency, K is small (reranking 20-50 docs, not 500), and your use case favors freshness over speed.

Pre-embed frequently accessed documents (”hot tier”), embed rarely-accessed documents on-the-fly (”cold tier”).

Access patterns follow Pareto distribution. 20% of docs get 80% of traffic.

Clear access patterns (some docs are accessed way more than others). Medium-to-large corpus (more than 100K documents). Mix of stable and changing content. Need good latency for common queries. Want to minimize re-embedding on model updates.

Fast for 80% of queries (hit pre-embedded cache). Fresh for rarely-accessed docs. Only re-embed hot tier when switching models (20% of corpus). Adapts to changing access patterns. Best latency/cost/flexibility trade-off.

Embed everything upfront. Store in vector database. Search with ANN (approximate nearest neighbors).

Very high query volume (more than 10K queries per day). Need under 50ms latency. Very stable corpus (under 5% churn per month). Access pattern is broad (no long tail). You have ML team to manage infrastructure.

Documents change frequently (more than 10% per week). You’re experimenting with embedding models. Low query volume (under 1K queries per day). You haven’t tried simpler approaches first.

This is where full pre-embedding hurts the most. When you need to switch models, you face downtime (your search is degraded while re-embedding), compute cost (re-embedding millions of documents), testing burden (full regression test suite on new embeddings), chunking reevaluation (maybe new model works better with different chunk sizes?), and risk (what if the new model is worse for your domain?).

This is overkill for most systems. I’ve seen teams spend months optimizing their vector database setup when query rewriting would have solved 90% of their problems.

But if you’re Pinterest, Shopify, or handling massive scale with a stable corpus, this is where you end up.

Here’s where things get spicy. We’ve been discussing single-intent queries: “How do I merge dataframes?”

But real users ask stuff like: “How do I read a CSV file, clean missing data, and plot the results?”

That’s three separate intents. Searching for this as one query is like trying to find a restaurant that serves pizza, sushi, and tacos. Good luck.

Modern agentic RAG systems (Perplexity, ChatGPT search) handle this elegantly:

Each sub-query is focused and precise, leading to better retrieval. Parallel execution means lower latency (max, not sum). Adaptive routing results in lower cost (only complex queries pay for LLM). Structured output provides better UX.

This is where agentic retrieval really shines. The agent can intelligently decide which sub-queries need expensive processing (embeddings) and which can be handled with cheap methods (simple preprocessing + BM25).

items.title: Netflix porta le Clip anche in Italia: nell'app arriva il feed di video verticali da scrollare
items.summary: Ogni Clip può essere utilizzata come punto di partenza per accedere al contenuto completo
items.content:
Netflix ha reso disponibile anche in Italia il nuovo design della sua app mobile, annunciato nei mesi scorsi e arrivato progressivamente nei diversi mercati. L'interfaccia è stata rivista per rendere più semplice la ricerca dei contenuti e introduce le Clip, un feed di brevi video verticali pensato soprattutto per chi utilizza il servizio dallo smartphone.

Al suo interno vengono mostrate scene e momenti salienti tratti da serie, film e speciali presenti nel catalogo. La selezione cambia in base ai gusti dell'utente e permette di scorrere rapidamente i diversi filmati fino a trovare qualcosa di interessante. Netflix vuole così ridurre il tempo trascorso tra copertine, categorie e schede dei titoli prima di decidere cosa vedere.

Ogni Clip può essere utilizzata come punto di partenza per accedere al contenuto completo. Dallo stesso schermo si può aggiungere un film o una serie a 'La mia lista', aprirne la scheda oppure condividere il video con altre persone attraverso le app di messaggistica e i social. La nuova sezione serve anche per riscoprire produzioni già presenti nel catalogo che potrebbero passare inosservate nella normale schermata iniziale.

​Il rinnovamento dell'app segue quello avviato lo scorso anno sui televisori, quando Netflix ha modificato la propria interfaccia TV per la prima volta dopo oltre dieci anni. Sullo smartphone la società ha scelto una navigazione più adatta all'utilizzo con una sola mano e alle consultazioni brevi, ad esempio durante una pausa o uno spostamento.

Netflix aveva presentato il nuovo design alla fine di aprile, avviando il rilascio negli Stati Uniti, nel Regno Unito, in Australia, Canada, India, Malesia, Pakistan, Filippine e Sudafrica. A luglio l'aggiornamento era arrivato anche in Brasile, Francia, Germania, Corea e Messico. Da oggi la distribuzione è stata estesa a tutti gli altri mercati.

Le Clip continueranno a essere ampliate nei prossimi mesi. Netflix prevede di aggiungere anche podcast, programmi trasmessi in diretta e raccolte dedicate a generi o interessi specifici, come le storie d'amore. L'obiettivo è trasformare la sezione in uno spazio dal quale scoprire buona parte dei contenuti disponibili sul servizio, compresi quelli da ascoltare o a cui giocare.

items.title: Far-right Israeli lawmaker damages Palestinian memorial with sledgehammer
items.summary: Zvi Sukkot's actions have drawn widespread condemnation, including from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
items.content:
A far-right member of the Israeli parliament has badly damaged a Palestinian memorial with a sledgehammer in the occupied West Bank while under military escort.

The incident has drawn strong criticism from Palestinians and across the political spectrum in Israel.

Video footage showed Zvi Sukkot, a member of the far-right Religious Zionism party, and several others striking the stone memorial in the Palestinian village of Madama.

In the video, Sukkot - who has a history of provocative anti-Palestinian acts - says: "This is something we cannot leave standing here, because any place that glorifies terrorism, we must remove it."

Rami Nasar, the head of the village council in Madama, said that the monument was erected in 2008 to remember Palestinians killed in the battle of Karameh - a day-long military confrontation between Israeli forces and those of both the PLO and Jordan in 1968.

It also memorialises Palestinians killed in the first and second intifada.

Nasar said it was intended to honour those who had been killed in conflict with Israel, whatever their political affiliation.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said its soldiers had been present during the incident. The Israeli military said it had approved a tour of monuments in the area for Sukkot and was providing security.

But the IDF said he and the others involved had acted deceptively and without authorisation.

It said soldiers eventually stopped Sukkot and escorted his group out of Madama after reporting the incident to their commanders.

In a number of previous incidents involving settler violence, soldiers have been filmed standing by without intervening.

The incident has further raised the temperature in the West Bank, where increasing attacks by settlers on Palestinians in recent months have drawn international condemnation.

Madama itself has been the target of several attacks by settlers.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office has issued a statement criticising Sukkot's actions. It read: "Taking the law into one's own hands, especially when it involves public figures, is a reprehensible practice that prevents the IDF from focusing on its missions of combating terrorism and incitement to violence."

Netanyahu's main rival in the upcoming general election, Gadi Eisenkot, said that Sukkot's behaviour was "a disgrace for anyone who claims to represent the public and be a leader".

Eisenkot also criticised Netanyahu for "allowing anarchists like Zvi Sukkot and his ilk to do whatever they please, endangering security in the settlements and harming Israel's standing in the world".

But finance minister Bezalel Smotrich - who heads the Religious Zionism party to which Sukkot belongs - directed his fiercest criticism at what he called the "frantic rush of the left-wing opposition to condemn Sukkot rather than terrorism itself".

On Monday, the most senior Israeli military officer in the West Bank, Major General Avi Bluth, was reported by Israeli media to have told Netanyahu in a closed-door meeting that the mounting violence by settlers could ignite a major escalation.

items.title: Nella Cina di Xi Jinping anche l’arte è un crimine
items.summary: La condanna al carcere dell’artista Gao Zhen dimostra che il presidente cinese non ha intenzione di fare la minima concessione a chi non rispetta le sue regole Leggi
items.content:
Forse qualcuno pensava che la Cina fosse al di sopra di certi comportamenti. D’altronde è la stessa Cina che impressiona con i suoi robot capaci di correre più veloci di Usain Bolt e che stupisce con la sua industria, la seconda al mondo e l’unica rivale di quella statunitense.

Ma nella Cina di Xi Jinping i vecchi riflessi sono duri a morire. Il 25 agosto Gao Zhen, artista cinese di settant’anni che è stato uno dei punti di riferimento dell’arte contemporanea pechinese, è stato condannato a tre anni di carcere al termine di un processo segreto.

Il suo crimine? Oltraggio agli eroi e ai martiri della rivoluzione cinese. L’aspetto più stravagante di questa vicenda è che Gao Zhen è stato condannato in base a una legge introdotta nel 2018, ma per opere che aveva realizzato in precedenza. In uno stato di diritto questo genere di retroattività non esiste. In Cina, evidentemente, la situazione è diversa.

Per anni Gao Zhen ha vissuto a New York, negli Stati Uniti, ma nell’estate 2024 era stato arrestato mentre si trovava in Cina per fare visita alla madre. Da allora è detenuto come un criminale, in alcuni momenti perfino in isolamento totale.

Insieme al fratello Qiang, l’artista formava un duo conosciuto come Gao brothers. I due erano stati stelle emergenti dell’arte negli anni novanta e duemila, in una scena spesso provocatoria che prendeva di mira i simboli di una Cina maoista che sembrava un brutto ricordo, sostituita da una società dei consumi molto meno ideologica.

Le opere dei fratelli Gao all’origine della condanna sono il riflesso di quell’epoca: un busto gigante e laccato di Mao con due enormi seni rossi, un Mao in ginocchio come un penitente e una scultura in cui alcuni soldati, tutti con il volto di Mao, sparano contro Gesù Cristo, dove è possibile leggere un riferimento al massacro di piazza Tiananmen .

La linea indicata da Xi è chiara: lo sviluppo economico e l’affermazione della potenza cinese non prevedono la minima concessione ideologica. Negli anni duemila molti si illudevano che la crescita economica avrebbe comportato inevitabilmente la liberalizzazione del sistema cinese. Era, appunto, un’illusione.

In quel periodo gli occidentali reagivano alla minima violazione dei diritti umani in Cina, nella speranza di spingere Pechino a rinunciare alle persecuzioni come quella di cui è stato vittima Gao Zhen. Ma era un’altra epoca. Oggi il rapporto di forze è cambiato e la Cina non tollera più questo genere di critiche. Il fatto che alla Casa Bianca ci sia un presidente statunitense che non ha la minima intenzione di sollevare un polverone sui diritti umani sicuramente aiuta.

Il 25 agosto le organizzazioni per la difesa dei diritti umani hanno espresso la loro incredulità dopo la condanna di Gao Zhen, che prima di essere rilasciato dovrà scontare ancora un anno di carcere. In molti hanno sottolineato che “l’arte non è un crimine”. A quanto pare, nella seconda potenza mondiale lo è eccome.

Internazionale pubblica ogni settimana una pagina di lettere. Ci piacerebbe sapere cosa pensi di questo articolo. Scrivici a: posta@internazionale.it

items.title: Libyan who was cleared after Lockerbie bombing trial dies aged 70
items.summary: A Facebook post by Libyan Airlines announced the death of Al Amin Khalifah Fhimah and expressed the company's condolences to his family.
items.content:
A Libyan who was cleared after standing trial over the Lockerbie bombing has died aged 70.

Al Amin Khalifah Fhimah was accused of murdering 270 people in the attack on Pan Am Flight 103 in December 1988.

He was found not guilty but a second Libyan, Abdulbasset Al Megrahi, was convicted of playing a key role in the bombing of the American airliner.

A Facebook post by Libyan Airlines announced Fhimah's death and expressed the company's condolences to his family.

Fhimah worked for the carrier in Malta before the bombing of Pan Am 103.

His funeral is set to take place on Wednesday in Tripoli, the capital of Libya.

The charges against Fhimah and Megrahi were first announced by Scotland and the United States in 1991.

Years of sanctions imposed on Libya by the United Nations led to the two men being handed over to stand trial at a Scottish court sitting in the Netherlands.

In 2001, three judges convicted Megrahi of mass murder and jailed him for life, but found Fhimah not guilty.

Megrahi died from cancer in 2012, after being freed on compassionate grounds by the Scottish government.

Fhimah always denied any involvement and was welcomed home to Libya by the country's late dictator Colonel Muammar Gaddafi.

In 2022, the FBI revealed that he had been implicated in the case again, through an alleged confession made by another Libyan who is facing trial in the United States.

Abu Agila Mohammad Masud Kheir Al-Marimi is said to have told a Libyan police officer that he took part in a plot to bomb the plane along with Fhimah and Megrahi, when all three were members of the Libyan intelligence service.

Al-Marimi has denied making the bomb that brought down the jumbo jet and claims the confession is false and was made under duress.

The contents of Al-Marimi's alleged confession and other new evidence which has emerged from Libya has led to speculation that Fhimah could have faced a second trial over the attack on the airliner.

The indictment against Fhimah announced by the US Government in 1991 is still outstanding.

Under the Double Jeopardy (Scotland) Act 2011 , external , a suspect can be tried over the same crime a second time, if there is new evidence - which was not available during the original trial - that substantially strengthens the case against them.

The BBC understands Scottish and US prosecutors would have looked at taking fresh action against Fhimah, if Al-Marimi was convicted by the court in Washington next year.

But pursuing a prosecution in Scotland or the US would have been legally challenging and politically sensitive, given his acquittal by the Scottish court in 2001.

On 21 December 1988, a plane explodes over Lockerbie, Scotland, killing 270 people. Almost four decades on, there's fresh evidence. Who was really behind the bombing?

Al Marimi is now due to stand trial in Washington in January, after a federal court judge agreed to postpone the case for a third time.

The delay, requested by the defence, followed the emergence of "newly discovered" evidence on the case.

The postponement was not connected to Fhimah's reported death.

Lockerbie bombing trial postponed days before it was due to start

items.title: Il più grande richiamo di auto in Cina, oltre 4 milioni. Dopo un incidente le maniglie di emergenza delle portiere sono difficili da trovare
items.summary: È il più grande richiamo automobilistico mai annunciato nel Paese. Le autorità contestano la difficoltà di individuare o azionare l’apertura meccanica d’emergenza in caso di incidente e guasto elettrico ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Tesla e altri otto costruttori richiameranno complessivamente circa 4,3 milioni di veicoli in Cina per problemi legati all’apertura delle portiere in situazioni di emergenza. Si tratta del più grande richiamo automobilistico mai registrato nel Paese. Il problema riguarda soprattutto le maniglie meccaniche di emergenza, che secondo le autorità cinesi possono essere difficili da individuare o utilizzare dopo un incidente grave , soprattutto se il sistema elettrico del veicolo smette di funzionare.

Le misure previste variano da semplici etichette informative a aggiornamenti software da remoto, fino a una migliore segnalazione dei punti da utilizzare per aprire manualmente le portiere.

Il richiamo più grande è quello di Tesla, che interessa 2,98 milioni di Model 3, Model Y, Model S e Model X, sia importate sia prodotte direttamente in Cina. La campagna partirà il 25 settembre.

Secondo quanto comunicato alla State Administration for Market Regulation, dopo una collisione particolarmente violenta e un’eventuale perdita di alimentazione elettrica, le maniglie meccaniche d’emergenza possono risultare poco intuitive da individuare. Questo potrebbe rallentare l’uscita degli occupanti o l’accesso dei soccorritori. Tesla applicherà gratuitamente delle etichette informative e distribuirà anche un aggiornamento software che, dopo un incidente, abbasserà automaticamente i finestrini.

Xiaomi richiamerà circa 390.000 veicoli, Leapmotor circa 371.000 e Xpeng circa 264.000. Anche Geely ha annunciato la propria campagna, mentre gli altri costruttori coinvolti hanno numeri molto più contenuti. Per Leapmotor, la correzione sarà relativamente semplice: ha spiegato che interverrà con una nuova etichetta di avvertimento e con un aggiornamento del software che controlla i finestrini elettrici. Le campagne rientrano comunque formalmente nella procedura di richiamo prevista dalle normative cinesi.

La questione delle maniglie a scomparsa e delle aperture elettroniche è diventata particolarmente delicata dopo diversi incidenti in cui gli occupanti sarebbero rimasti intrappolati all’interno di veicoli in fiamme.

A ottobre, i media di Stato cinesi avevano riferito della morte del conducente di una Xiaomi SU7 dopo un incidente seguito da un incendio. Secondo quelle ricostruzioni, alcune persone presenti sul posto non sarebbero riuscite ad aprire le portiere per estrarre il guidatore. La crescente diffusione di sistemi elettronici per l’apertura delle portiere ha spinto il governo cinese ad aumentare la pressione sui costruttori.

Il governo ha già stabilito che dal 2027 saranno vietate le maniglie completamente nascoste, rendendo la Cina il primo Paese a eliminare progressivamente una soluzione resa popolare proprio da Tesla e poi adottata da molti produttori di auto elettriche.

Nonostante i numeri molto elevati, il costo complessivo del richiamo potrebbe essere relativamente contenuto. Una parte significativa degli interventi infatti potrà essere effettuata tramite aggiornamenti software a distanza, senza richiedere il passaggio delle vetture in officina.

Anche le modifiche fisiche previste, come l’aggiunta di etichette e indicazioni più chiare, non dovrebbero richiedere interventi particolarmente costosi.

items.title: OpenAI mostra i muscoli di Jalapeño: il chip “fatto in casa” batte Nvidia nei primi test
items.summary: OpenAI ha pubblicato i primi benchmark di Jalapeño. Fino a 3,6 volte meno latenza rispetto ai sistemi Nvidia e quasi il doppio dei token elaborati per ogni kW ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
OpenAI ha diffuso i primi risultati misurati di Jalapeño, il chip ASIC (un circuito integrato progettato per un solo compito, in questo caso l'inferenza) “fatto in casa” e annunciato a giugno insieme a Broadcom. Secondo OpenAI un sistema diretto da Jalapeño restituisce risposte più rapide e sostiene più lavoro per ogni watt consumato rispetto ai migliori acceleratori oggi disponibili, senza il compromesso tra velocità e capacità che di norma grava sull'hardware da data center.

I test sono stati condotti su InferenceX, una piattaforma di benchmark pubblica sviluppata da SemiAnalysis che misura l'intero ciclo di una richiesta a un LLM.

Nel suo comunicato , che ovviamente tiene conto solo dei suoi test interni senza verificatori terzi, OpenAI dice di aver posizionato Jalapeño sulla “Pareto frontier” , cioè la curva che raccoglie le combinazioni ottimali di due grandezze in conflitto tra loro, in questo caso throughput (il volume di lavoro svolto) e latenza (il tempo di risposta). Generalmente, un sistema sul fronte di Pareto non può migliorare ulteriormente una delle due grandezze senza peggiorare l’altra; i sistemi meno efficienti si collocano invece al di fuori della frontiera, perché esistono configurazioni capaci di batterli su almeno una delle due metriche senza penalizzare l’altra.

I numeri che hanno mostrato i muscoli di Jalapeño riguardano tre modelli: GPT-OSS 120B (il modello a pesi aperti di OpenAI stessa), DeepSeek R1 e Kimi K2.5 da 1.000 miliardi di parametri, il più grande dei tre.

Su GPT-OSS 120B Jalapeño raggiunge quasi il doppio dei token elaborati per kilowatt al picco (85.448 contro 44.960) e completa una richiesta in 1,03 secondi contro 1,80.

Su DeepSeek R1 il vantaggio in latenza sale a 3,6 volte (1,65 contro 5,99 secondi).

Su Kimi K2.5, il modello più pesante, il margine si riduce a circa 1,5 volte in efficienza per watt e 3,4 volte in latenza.

C’è un fatto curioso. Nel testo del comunicato, OpenAI non nomina mai i sistemi con cui Jalapeño è stato confrontato . Solo nelle didascalie dei grafici in appendice emergono i nomi reali: le due superchip Nvidia GB200 (Blackwell) e GB300 (Blackwell Ultra) .

Emerge anche il dato sui consumi, altrettanto assente dal corpo del testo: Jalapeño è certificato per 700 watt ma nei carichi testati si è fermato a 550 watt misurati, contro i 1.200 watt di GB200 e i 1.400 di GB300 .

Richard Ho, vicepresidente hardware di OpenAI, ha detto ai giornalisti durante un briefing che i sistemi IA "devono di solito scegliere" tra bassa latenza e alto throughput, mentre Jalapeño offrirebbe entrambi.

A proposito di Nvidia, ha anche escluso che il nuovo chip sostituisca l'intero parco hardware dell'azienda. Nvidia resta, nelle sue parole, "un partner molto valido".

La distribuzione in piccoli volumi è prevista entro fine 2026, con una crescita nel 2027, come già indicato da Broadcom, fino alla piena operatività attesa nella prima metà del 2028.

Resta aperta la questione di chi abbia "effettivamente" progettato Jalapeño. A giugno l'ingegnere Google Patrick Toulme aveva ipotizzato un contributo pesante di modelli OpenAI interni nello sviluppo.

In un nuovo intervento su X, Toulme ha sostenuto che dietro il chip ci sarebbe GPT-Astra, il nome in codice con cui OpenAI indica il suo prossimo modello di punta, ancora non rilasciato pubblicamente e finora associato soprattutto alla soluzione di problemi matematici irrisolti.

Secondo Toulme, OpenAI avrebbe addestrato con reinforcement learning modelli interni per scrivere il codice RTL del chip (i kernel in linguaggio assembly per il proprio set di istruzioni), e persino un simulatore ciclo-accurato del processore che avrebbe permesso di testare le ottimizzazioni su normali CPU, senza disporre ancora del chip fisico. Sono ipotesi non confermate da OpenAI, che finora ha solo dichiarato di essere rimasta sorpresa dal contributo dei propri modelli allo sviluppo di Jalapeño .

items.title: Meeting di Rimini, l'incontro 'Europa. Custodire le radici, accelerare il futuro' con Roberta Metsola
items.summary: La diretta su ANSA.it dalle 12
items.content:
Al Meeting di Rimini incontro con Roberta Metsola, presidente del Parlamento Europeo . Intervento di saluto di Antonio Tajani, vicepresidente Consiglio dei Ministri, ministro degli Esteri e della Cooperazione Internazionale.

Introduce Bernhard Scholz, presidente Fondazione Meeting per l’amicizia fra i popoli ETS

L’Europa non ha il lusso del tempo: decisioni più rapide, un mercato unico compiuto, un bilancio all’altezza delle sfide. Ma la vera forza dell’Unione nasce da radici più antiche, l’incontro fra tradizione greco-romana, giudaico-cristiana e pensiero liberale e sociale, da cui discendono la dignità della persona, lo Stato di diritto, l’universalità dei diritti. Allargarsi restando fedeli a sé stessi, accelerare senza smarrire la memoria, dentro circostanze storiche complesse. Un’Europa insieme più grande e più vera.

items.title: Pizzaballa: 'Momento molto duro, arginare la deriva estremista'
items.summary: "I fatti sembrano smentire ogni attesa di cambiamento ma non dobbiamo arrenderci"
items.content:
"Stiamo vivendo in un tempo molto duro per la vita di moltissime famiglie, non solo a Gaza, ma anche in Cisgiordania, dove la paura è determinante. I fatti sembrano smentire ogni attesa di cambiamento, ma non dobbiamo nemmeno arrenderci, perché significa lasciare il discorso a questi estremisti. Dobbiamo fare tutto il possibile a livello locale, nazionale e internazionale, dal mio punto di vista più religioso che politico, per tenere viva l'attenzione e per cercare di arginare questa deriva". Lo dice il cardinale Patriarca di Gerusalemme, Pierbattista Pizzaballa, a ilSussidiario, anticipando i temi del suo intervento al Meeting.

Nella situazione difficile che si vive a Gaza e in Cisgiordania ci sono tuttavia dei "barlumi che aprono a una realtà ancora afferrabile", ha aggiunto Pizzaballa. "Siamo nel tempo dell'attesa, purtroppo. Attesa di decisioni che si devono prendere, sia politiche - ha sottolineato il Patriarca - che di altro genere. È un tempo molto difficile, perché è un'attesa molto lunga e la sfida che affrontiamo è riempire questa attesa non di delusione, frustrazione o di rabbia, ma insieme a quelli che io definisco frammenti di umanità, dobbiamo tenere viva questa attesa nella speranza che questa promessa si compia quanto prima".

items.summary: L'azzurro e la svizzera accedono alla semifinale dello slam americano
items.content:
Flavio Cobolli e Belinda Bencic mettono in fila un'altra vittoria e accedono alla semifinale del doppio misto nello Us Open eliminando la coppia formata da Carlos Alcaraz e Serena Williams. L'azzurro e la svizzera hanno avuto la meglio in due set, con il risultato finale di 5-4 (7-4) 4-1, maturato dopo 56 minuti di gioco.

La giornata ha regalato momenti di divertimento e siparietti improvvisati fra le diverse coppie impegnate nel torneo (quasi una sorta di esibizione con set al meglio dei quattro game). Un quartetto da sogno prima dell'inizio degli US Open di domenica, che ha offerto a Federer "una vera opportunità per dire grazie e addio".

items.title: Indian jewellery ad pulled after backlash over actor's outfit
items.summary: Kriti Sanon has defended the ad in which she was seen celebrating the upcoming Hindu festival of Rakhi.
items.content:
An Indian jewellery brand has removed their new advertisement for the upcoming festival of Rakshabandhan, also known as Rakhi, after backlash over the outfit worn by the female lead.

The ad featured popular Bollywood actor Kriti Sanon celebrating the Hindu festival in which sisters tie a thread called Rakhi over their brothers' wrists.

Sanon, who is seen in a cropped top, skirt and a cape, addressed her critics on Tuesday night saying "culture and traditions are in a woman's heart, not in her neckline!"

The row started earlier on Tuesday after actor and BJP MP Kangana Ranaut called the ad "intentionally creepy" and asked why someone would tie a Rakhi dressed in a bikini.

In her comments posted on social media, Ranaut did not name Sanon, but appeared to be referring to the actor.

"It is a wonderful time to be a woman, our closets are full of variety of clothes... From all the options that are available to us today why would you tie your brother a Rakhi in your bikini/under garments? Where are all your styling options? The advert looks intentionally creepy," she wrote.

Her remarks quickly drew attention online, with some users echoing her criticism of Sanon's outfit saying it was too revealing and inappropriate for a traditional festival.

One commentator described her top as a bralette, saying there was a "clear line between modern styling and basic sensitivity towards Hindu festivals".

"Pairing a bralette outfit with a sacred occasion like Rakshabandhan felt completely out of touch and unnecessary," she posted on X.

Others objected to a scene in the advertisement in which the actor also ties a rakhi on her pet dog.

But Sanon also received support, including from Congress MP Rahul Gandhi, who defended her, saying what a woman chose to wear was her own decision. Others accused Ranaut of moral policing.

Some also pointed out that though Ranaut has been more conservative in her clothing in recent years after becoming a politician, she herself often wore short dresses and Western outfits in her films and at social gatherings.

Sanon responded to the critics in an Instagram story, calling out the mindset that questioned women for their sartorial choices. Like Ranaut, she did not name anyone directly.

"The essence of festivals is not in the clothes you wear, it is in the emotions and meaning you hold for the traditions... When will we stop telling women what to wear?? Ethnic fashion has evolved over the years, but still a woman's respect for her culture is measured with just her clothes!! Culture & Traditions are in her heart, not in her neckline!"

Sanon also addressed the issue of tying Rakhi to her pet, saying though the festival traditionally celebrates the bond between a brother and sister, its spirit was about protecting loved ones - which, for her, included her sister and her pet.

Despite her spirited defence, jewellery company Giva announced on Wednesday it was pulling the ad.

"We have the highest regard and deep respect for Indian culture, traditions and festivals. As a brand, we have always believed in celebrating these joyous moments with the entire family and this time we wanted to extend the love and celebration to our pets," Giva said in a statement , external on Instagram.

The Indian woman who stood up to moral policing - and won a pageant

Assam shorts: India teenager forced to cover legs with curtain at exam centre

"If our recent advertisement has inadvertently hurt the sentiments of some segments of society, that was not our intent at all. Out of respect, we have withdrawn the advertisement from all media," it added.

Giva is not the first Indian brand to withdraw an ad after criticism on social media. In 2020, popular jewellery brand Tanishq withdrew an advertisement featuring an interfaith couple after it faced right-wing backlash online.

Debates over what women should - and shouldn't - wear have also repeatedly sparked controversy in India.

Last year, a beauty pageant contestant was commended for standing up to a group of men who tried to bully her and other contestants over the skirts and western dresses they were wearing.

In 2021, there was outrage after a 19-year-old student, who turned up in shorts to take an exam, was forced to wrap a curtain around her legs after the teacher objected to her clothes.

In the same year, thousands of women - and some men - shared photos of themselves wearing ripped jeans after the chief minister of the northern state of Uttarakhand criticised a woman for wearing them.

items.title: Cover IA di Like a Prayer di Madonna scala le classifiche, scatta la stretta in Australia
items.summary: Al bando le canzoni create in toto o prevalentemente con l'intelligenza artificiale
items.content:
Una cover IA di 'Like a Prayer' di Madonna fa scattare la stretta in Australia contro l'uso dell'intelligenza artificiale come strumento primario nella produzione di canzoni. Secondo diversi media statunitensi, l'Aria, l'Australian Recording Industry Association, ha ufficialmente escluso i brani generati interamente o prevalentemente con l'intelligenza artificiale dalle sue classifiche musicali ufficiali. Lo scopo è promuovere la natura umana dell'arte.

La svolta è arrivata dopo le polemiche sul successo virale di una cover del brano 'Like A Prayer'. Il pezzo, realizzato dal DJ australiano Josh Fawaz con l'ausilio di strumenti di IA come il software Suno per voci e batteria, ha scalato le classifiche radiofoniche e di vendita locali ed è stato ascoltato oltre 48 milioni di volte su Spotify.

L'uso dell'IA non è del tutto bandito: gli artisti possono ancora usarla tecnicamente come parte del processo creativo, ma il brano deve essere stato scritto da esseri umani e la voce principale e gli strumenti primari devono essere affidati a persone. "Gli artisti già usano strumenti di IA nel loro lavoro; le classifiche possono e devono evolvere per fare spazio alla nuova realtà, ma la musica generata totalmente da servizi costruiti sulle registrazioni degli artisti è tutta un'altra questione", ha sottolineato la direttrice generale di Aria, Annabelle Herd.

items.title: Bodies found on S Korean holiday island as missing persons scandal deepens
items.summary: A police sergeant has been arrested following accusations that he lied to victims' families and prematurely closed missing persons cases.
items.content:
Four missing people have been found dead on South Korean holiday island Jeju, as local police face mounting public criticism for allegedly mishandling missing persons cases.

Reports emerged last week that authorities were launching a belated search for a woman reported missing months ago. This sparked criticism of the police for failing to search for her earlier.

The scandal has since deepened with the arrest of a police sergeant, surnamed Bu, who is accused of lying to victims' families and prematurely closing missing persons cases.

Four officers in the sergeant's chain of command have been put on administrative leave and on Tuesday President Lee Jae Myung ordered a sweeping reform of the police force.

Since Saturday, police have found four bodies on the island, including that of 37-year-old Jang Mi-ran who had gone missing in May.

On Monday, her body was located at a palm tree farm about 500 metres (547 yards) from where she was staying. She was believed to have killed herself.

Bu is suspected to have closed Jang's case prematurely without confirming her whereabouts.

According to local reports, Bu had allegedly told Jang's boyfriend that he had spoken to Jang over the phone and she had told Bu she did not wish to speak to her boyfriend.

Police also found the body of a man in his 60s from Jeju City on Saturday.

The man had gone missing on 28 June. Bu had closed his case and reportedly told the family that the man was found "safe" but "does not wish to disclose his location to the family".

"We believed the police when they said my father was safe and waited, but after 51 days, what returned was his body," the man's son told reporters.

It is not yet clear whether Bu was involved in the missing persons cases for two other bodies that were found in coastal villages in recent days.

Police are now examining all the missing persons reports that Bu had handled, which number nearly 300.

Jeju is one of South Korea's most popular tourist destinations.

The island, known for its rows of palm trees and sparkling waters, received more than 13 million foreign and domestic visitors last year.

While violent crime is rare in South Korea, suicide rates are among the highest in the world.

Some experts have said the low crime rate is part of the reason why missing persons cases are not taken seriously.

"After experiencing on the field that the absolute majority of missing adults are found quickly, [the officers] tend to assume all cases are like that," Lee Yung-hyeock, a professor specialising in police science at Konkuk University, told Yonhap news agency.

While more than 70,000 adults are reported missing in South Korea each year, 99% of them are marked as resolved within a month.

On Tuesday, President Lee said during a Cabinet meeting that "the recent breakdown in police discipline and irresponsibility in public safety matters have become serious problems".

Pointing out that the police are likely to wield the most power out of all the state's institutions, he said "the Korean people are questioning whether [the police] deserve this large power".

South Korea's national police chief was grilled by lawmakers at an emergency National Assembly hearing on Monday, during which he admitted that "there is a fault in the system".

This scandal comes at a politically sensitive time for South Korea's police.

The government had recently passed reform to transfer full investigative power from the prosecutors to the police, a move they said was intended to curtail the prosecutors' influence in politics.

However, the reform has been unpopular among the public, who have for many years accused the police of corruption and incompetence.

items.title: Cento scatti in finale al Wildlife Photographer of the Year
items.summary: Record di candidature, con oltre 65mila foto da 121 Paesi. I vincitori il 13 ottobre
items.content: Un orso polare che scruta il foro nella banchisa creato da una foca per respirare. Un rondone che vola a bassa quota sotto la sagoma di un aereo in arrivo all'aeroporto di Heathrow. Un rospo che passeggia per le strade di Tokyo dopo un acquazzone. Sono solo alcune delle 100 immagini finaliste alla 62esima edizione del Wildlife Photographer of the Year , il più prestigioso concorso di fotografia naturalistica al mondo promosso dal Natural History Museum di Londra, che decreterà i vincitori il prossimo 13 ottobre. Il concorso, che racconta la bellezza e la diversità della natura richiamando l'attenzione sulle minacce che mettono a rischio specie e habitat , ha ricevuto quest'anno un numero record di candidature , con oltre 65mila scatti provenienti da 121 Paesi e territori. Le foto finaliste sono state selezionate da una giuria internazionale di esperti di fotografia naturalistica, cinema, scienza e conservazione, valutandone creatività, originalità, eccellenza tecnica e capacità di raccontare storie legate al mondo naturale. L'intera serie sarà esposta in una mostra al museo londinese a partire da venerdì 16 ottobre . Le immagini saranno accompagnate da contenuti dedicati ai cambiamenti degli habitat naturali, con approfondimenti sul Biodiversity Intactness Index , l'indicatore sviluppato dal Natural History Museum per misurare quanta parte della biodiversità originaria di una regione rimane intatta. L'indice è stato adottato come indicatore ufficiale del Global Biodiversity Framework per monitorare i cambiamenti della biodiversità e i progressi nella conservazione della natura.
